## Appearance

Paul Irving is distinguished by his serious blue eyes and a head of brown curls.

_Sources: [v2 XXVII An Afternoon at the Stone House P29](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0029), [v2 XXVII An Afternoon at the Stone House P30](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0030)_

## Personality

Paul Irving is described as a fair-minded, clean, and manly young boy who behaves like a perfect little gentleman. Highly imaginative, poetic, and regarded as a genius, he frequently thinks strange, beautiful thoughts and excels at telling elaborate stories.

_Sources: [v2 VII The Pointing of Duty P7](../source/v02-c07.md#nw-v02-c07-p0007), [v2 VIII Marilla Adopts Twins P32](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0032), [v2 VIII Marilla Adopts Twins P52](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0052), [v2 XI Facts and Fancies P38](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0038), [v2 XVIII An Adventure on the Tory Road P3](../source/v02-c18.md#nw-v02-c18-p0003), [v2 XIX Just a Happy Day P33](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0033), +2 more_

## History

Paul Irving was an imaginative motherless boy who lived near the shore with his grandmother and only grew close to his father after his mother died three years prior. Upon joining the [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) school, he quickly formed a bond with his teacher, [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md), cheering her up with wild orchids on her first day of teaching and sharing his vibrant imagination through a letter describing fictional rock friends. Over the school year, he connected deeply with [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) over memory and grief in the graveyard, and he later hosted her for tea at his house. During a visit to [Echo Lodge](../codex/places.md#echo-lodge), Paul bonded with Miss [Lavendar](../character/lavendar-lewis.md) over their shared experiences with imaginary dream-people, and he later visited [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) while helping Miss [Lavendar](../character/lavendar-lewis.md) prepare for her wedding.

_Sources: [v2 V A Full-fledged Schoolma’am P0](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0000), [v2 V A Full-fledged Schoolma’am P7](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0007), [v2 V A Full-fledged Schoolma’am P13](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0013), [v2 V A Full-fledged Schoolma’am P20](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0020), [v2 XI Facts and Fancies P0](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0000), [v2 XI Facts and Fancies P9](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0009), +43 more_

## Quotes

> "and I came back to give them to you because I thought you were the kind of lady that would like them, and because . . ."
>
> — Paul Irving — [v2 V A Full-fledged Schoolma’am P21](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0021)

> “Yes; but if dryads are foolish they must take the consequences, just as if they were real people,” said Paul gravely. “Do you know what I think about the new moon, teacher? I think it is a little golden boat full of dreams.”
>
> — Paul Irving — [v2 XIX Just a Happy Day P30](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0030)

> "I’ve eaten enough to make anyone grow. I do hope, now that I’ve begun, I’ll keep on till I’m as tall as father. He is six feet, you know, Miss Lavendar."
>
> — Paul Irving — [v2 XXVII An Afternoon at the Stone House P24](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0024)

> "I think you would make a splendid mother. You have just the right look in your eyes . . . the look my little mother always had. I think it’s a pity you haven’t any boys of your own."
>
> — Paul Irving — [v2 XXVII An Afternoon at the Stone House P58](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0058)

> "He knows I won’t associate with him if he doesn’t. He is really full of wickedness, I think."
>
> — Paul Irving — [v2 XV The Beginning of Vacation P14](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0014)

## Relationships

### [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/anne-shirley--paul-irving.md)

Paul is a student of [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md), who acts as an influential teacher in his life. Beyond their dynamic in the classroom, the two share a close bond as kindred spirits and confidants. They spend time walking together to share their feelings on grief, memory, and imagination, and Paul cheers [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) up after school by bringing her wild orchids or inviting her over for tea to talk about his imaginative ideas.

_Sources: [v2 I An Irate Neighbor P45](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0045), [v2 V A Full-fledged Schoolma’am P8](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0008), [v2 VII The Pointing of Duty P7](../source/v02-c07.md#nw-v02-c07-p0007), +13 more_
